review_reason: The ACL xattr payload allocation uses GFP_NOFS and may fail; ext4_get_acl returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM).
posix_acl_alloc allocates the decoded ACL with GFP_NOFS; a failed allocation is returned as ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM).
Quota initialization can fail while loading quota data; ext4_set_acl returns the error before starting the ACL update.

The helper returns an error only for an unknown ACL tag (fs/posix_acl.c:339). The VFS setter validates the ACL at fs/posix_acl.c:951, and the ext4 decoder rejects unknown tags at fs/ext4/acl.c:74 before the chmod path uses the ACL.
Deriving inherited ACLs can fail while querying or cloning the directory ACL; inode ACL initialization returns that error.
GFP_NOFS allocation for the serialized ACL can fail; conversion returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM).

The call uses __GFP_NOFAIL through include/linux/buffer_head.h:378. This path rejects out-of-range bitmap blocks at fs/ext4/balloc.c:480, and mount validates filesystem size against the backing device at fs/ext4/super.c:4746. The NULL branch is defensive for the validated geometry.
The lock-state query lets prefetch discard its reference to a buffer whose I/O is already in progress.
A cached up-to-date buffer avoids submission of a read; a false bit requests I/O, rather than reporting its failure.
The wrapper combines two ordinary bitmap-cache validity bits to tell callers whether to fetch the bitmap.
If trylock contends, ext4_lock_group updates a contention counter and takes the blocking path.
The buffer lock bit is checked only as an initialization assertion.
A previously verified bitmap avoids duplicate validation on this early path.
The recheck under the group lock lets a prior verification bypass checksum computation.
BH_New indicates whether this path must wait for bitmap I/O; a clear bit returns success.
After waiting for the submitted block-bitmap read, a clear BH_Uptodate identifies a failed read. The caller reports the error, marks the block bitmap corrupt and returns -EIO.
wait_on_buffer reads the lock bit to decide whether it needs to sleep for the buffer.
Group membership is a credential predicate used to decide access to reserved clusters.
The test reads the bitmap's own allocation bit. A clear bit is corrupt input data, not a failure of test_bit_le.
The test reads whether the inode bitmap block is marked allocated. A false value comes from metadata contents.
Allocation of the system-zone descriptor can fail under memory pressure and aborts setup with -ENOMEM.
The slab allocation for the protected region can fail; insertion stops and propagates -ENOMEM.
No predecessor is an ordinary tree boundary; the optional adjacent-zone merge is skipped.
The directory entry name allocation can fail and ext4_htree_store_dirent returns -ENOMEM.

The on-disk EXT4_ENCRYPT_FL becomes S_ENCRYPTED at fs/ext4/inode.c:4601 even in this build. The directory open callback can succeed, then readdir returns -EOPNOTSUPP from the disabled fscrypt stub at include/linux/fscrypt.h:769.
The allocation branch requires S_ENCRYPTED. With CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION off, fscrypt_prepare_readdir has already returned -EOPNOTSUPP for that inode at fs/ext4/dir.c:138.
The task signal query cannot fail. ext4 uses its true result to cancel readdir with -ERESTARTSYS and free temporary state.
An index outside the current readahead window can trigger ordinary synchronous readahead.
The bit only determines whether to verify the checksum. A checksum mismatch is a separate operation and result.
Filename conversion requires an encrypted directory. With CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION off, fscrypt_prepare_readdir rejects that directory before the scan at fs/ext4/dir.c:138.
The private directory state allocation can fail; the open callback returns -ENOMEM without installing that state.
Starting the reserved JBD2 handle can fail on an aborted journal; ext4 converts the negative status to ERR_PTR.
An active handle can become aborted, including when its journal aborts. This check rejects the credit request with -EROFS before attempting any journal extension.
Journal write access can be denied on an aborted handle; the wrapper aborts the handle as needed and propagates the error.
This reports whether abort has already happened, preventing duplicate abort work and messages.
A journal revoke can return an actual error; ext4 aborts the handle, reports the filesystem error and propagates the status.
Create access can return -EROFS on an abort; ext4 records the abort and returns the JBD2 error.
JBD2 can return -EROFS when an abort races with marking metadata dirty (fs/jbd2/transaction.c:1538). The ext4 wrapper returns err even if an already aborted handle suppresses additional diagnostics.
This is a query of an existing handle abort, used to suppress secondary reporting around a prior JBD2 failure.
BH_Req records that a request occurred. It gates the subsequent inspection of the earlier write, without independently failing.
In the synchronous no-journal path, the buffer has been submitted and the completed write can leave BH_Uptodate clear. This check reports the metadata write failure and returns -EIO.
The extent-cache traversal array uses fallible GFP_NOFS; ext4 drops i_data_sem before returning -ENOMEM.
This buffer lookup can allocate with GFP_NOFS and without EXT4_EX_NOFAIL on ordinary traversal; failure gives ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) to the tree walk.
A false result means a cache buffer is now locked and needs a read; ext4_read_bh performs the fallible operation next.
The verification cache bit can bypass extent metadata validation, but it cannot fail independently.
The default extent-path allocation uses fallible GFP_NOFS and reports ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM); only callers passing EXT4_EX_NOFAIL avoid this failure.
The i_data_sem state only feeds a WARN_ON lock precondition.
The array request uses GFP_NOFS | __GFP_NOFAIL. The extent depth is bounded by EXT4_MAX_EXTENT_DEPTH, so the array size cannot overflow. The NULL check is defensive for this request.
An already-aborted handle causes the helper to skip saving the fsync transaction ID; this is a state read.
The proposed fallocate growth can exceed RLIMIT_FSIZE; ext4_fallocate unwinds through out and returns the size-check error.
VFS privilege or timestamp update can return an error; fallocate takes its unlock path without allocating file blocks.
A privilege or timestamp update may fail before collapsing the range; the error is preserved through out_mutex.
A privilege or timestamp update may fail before inserting the range; the error is preserved through out_mutex.
Extending the file in zero range can exceed RLIMIT_FSIZE; ext4 exits through out_mutex before preallocation.
VFS metadata preparation can fail; zero range leaves by out_mutex before preallocating or zeroing.

The ioctl passes user-specified length, start and flags. fiemap_prep can return -EINVAL, -EFBIG or -EBADR from validation, or a writeback error when FIEMAP_FLAG_SYNC is set (fs/ioctl.c:175). ext4 returns the error before traversing extents.

Copying a non-final extent to userspace can return -EFAULT (fs/ioctl.c:145). The caller checks and propagates that error when a following extent exists. The final-record branch exits before checking err.
The inode1 extent semaphore state is used only in a BUG_ON invariant.
The inode2 extent semaphore state is used only in a BUG_ON invariant.
The inode1 lock-state predicate enforces a BUG_ON precondition before swapping extents.
The inode2 lock-state predicate enforces a BUG_ON precondition before swapping extents.
The wrapper only returns the inode semaphore state for callers' checks.
The bookkeeping array allocation is fallible without EXT4_EX_NOFAIL; the split returns -ENOMEM before allocating tree blocks.
The new leaf's buffer-cache allocation uses fallible GFP_NOFS; NULL goes to cleanup to release resources from the split.

The block was allocated as ext4 metadata at fs/ext4/extents.c:1112. sb_getblk uses __GFP_NOFAIL through include/linux/buffer_head.h:378, so the NULL cleanup is defensive for valid allocator output and mounted device geometry.
The cleanup tests whether to unlock a non-NULL buffer before releasing it; this lock-state query cannot fail.
Buffer-cache allocation for the new tree block uses fallible GFP_NOFS and NULL is propagated as -ENOMEM.
The inode lock-state check only supplies a WARN_ON_ONCE before an ordinary size update.

The slab allocation uses fallible GFP_ATOMIC. When it returns NULL, __es_insert_extent returns -ENOMEM at fs/ext4/extents_status.c:833. Delayed extent insertion drops the lock and retries with blocking preallocation at fs/ext4/extents_status.c:2122.
The blocking extent-status preallocation requests __GFP_NOFAIL for a fixed-size object.

The slab allocation uses fallible GFP_ATOMIC. A NULL result becomes -ENOMEM at fs/ext4/extents_status.c:1990. Delayed extent insertion can drop the lock and retry with blocking pending-reservation preallocation at fs/ext4/extents_status.c:2125.
The blocking pending-reservation preallocation requests __GFP_NOFAIL for a fixed-size object.
Allocation for the first per-CPU counter can fail; shrinker registration returns before installing any counters.
Allocation for the cache-miss counter can fail; err1 destroys the already initialized hit counter.
Allocation for the total extent counter can fail; err2 unwinds the earlier cache counters.
Allocation for the shrinkable extent counter can fail; err3 unwinds the previously initialized counters.
The shrinker allocation may return NULL; registration sets -ENOMEM and destroys its already constructed counters.
No predecessor means there is no left extent to merge; the original extent is returned.
The first list-state test skips inserting an inode already on the extent shrink list.
The second list-state test under lock prevents duplicate insertion into the shrink list.
The predecessor is used only if present; NULL represents the left boundary for reservation accounting.
The reverse scan stops normally when no preceding extent remains.
An empty shrink list is an ordinary end of the reclaim scan; the code unlocks and exits.
A contended trylock only defers this inode in the reclaim scan and increments nr_skipped.
Converts the elapsed time for a statistic; neither its value nor the averaging branch is an error.
The result decides whether to emit the warning at this time; rate-limit suppression is ordinary behavior.
Only a linked inode is removed from the shrink list and decrements the list count.
An inode without fast-commit tracking simply bypasses the update synchronization.
The inode fast-commit queue's emptiness contributes to the early no-work return.
The inode dentry queue's emptiness contributes to the early no-work return.
A linked inode is removed from the fast-commit queue; no list membership is a routine state.
The empty dentry queue means there is no fast-commit dentry entry to clean up.
The queue predicate supports a warning about the expected post-removal state.
A transaction-ID comparison updates the latest fast-commit ineligibility marker.
The list test prevents enqueueing a tracked inode twice in fast commit.
Allocation of the tracking node can fail; ext4 marks fast commit ineligible, reacquires the mutex and returns -ENOMEM.
The long-name allocation can fail; ext4 releases the entry, marks fast commit ineligible and returns -ENOMEM with the mutex restored.
A per-inode dentry-list predicate serves the create-reference invariant warning.
The atomic read snapshots the subtransaction ID to compare later if another commit is active.
An aborted journal can make jbd2_fc_begin_commit return -EIO (fs/jbd2/journal.c:699). The caller records commit start failure and attempts a full transaction commit.
The atomic read checks whether the subtransaction ID advanced while another commit was running.
The ID comparison decides whether a concurrent commit already reached the requested transaction.
jbd2_fc_wait_bufs returns -EIO when a submitted journal buffer did not complete successfully; ext4 takes the full-commit fallback.
Growing the replay allocation-region array may fail; the replay bookkeeping callback returns -ENOMEM.
Compares the completed transaction ID to the inode sync ID to reset or retain fast-commit state.
The fast-commit dentry queue is drained until the ordinary empty condition.
The transaction-ID comparison decides whether the fast-commit ineligibility marker can be cleared.
Reads the count of active inode updates to decide whether the commit needs to wait.
Rechecks the update count after preparing the wait to avoid sleeping after the last update completed.
Submitting the tracked inode's data can fail in the writeback callback; ext4 returns the error and leaves the fast-commit path.
Waiting for inode writeback can report an I/O error; ext4 returns it to the fast-commit caller.
An empty main dentry queue avoids unnecessary fast-commit record preparation.
The list-state check only supports a warning when a create record lacks its expected inode reference.
Acquiring an initial buffer can fail because the journal fast-commit area is full or the block mapping fails (fs/jbd2/journal.c:840). ext4 propagates NULL to abort the fast-commit attempt.
Acquiring the next buffer after submitting the previous one can hit the fast-commit area limit or a block mapping error (fs/jbd2/journal.c:840). ext4 propagates NULL to abort the fast-commit attempt.
d_alloc can fail to allocate the replay dentry; ext4 records -ENOMEM and follows out to release acquired references.
The modified-inode replay array growth can fail; the old pointer is preserved and the caller gets -ENOMEM.
list_splice_init tests whether the source list has entries to splice and reinitialize.
SEEK_HOLE at or beyond EOF can return -ENXIO, and extent mapping can return an error (fs/iomap/seek.c:45). ext4 releases the shared inode lock and propagates the negative result.
SEEK_DATA can return -ENXIO when no data remains, and extent mapping can return an error (fs/iomap/seek.c:96). ext4 releases the shared inode lock and propagates the negative result.

Existing encrypted files retain S_ENCRYPTED from on-disk inode flags at fs/ext4/inode.c:4601. An encrypted file can have an unencrypted parent. If open reaches this stub, it returns -EOPNOTSUPP at include/linux/fscrypt.h:736 and ext4 propagates it.
Existing verity files retain S_VERITY from on-disk inode flags at fs/ext4/inode.c:4605. The disabled fsverity stub at include/linux/fsverity.h:212 then returns -EOPNOTSUPP and ext4 propagates it.
A busy inode causes shared lock acquisition to fail for IOCB_NOWAIT; direct read returns -EAGAIN.

The wrapper directly forwards down_read_trylock's acquisition failure to both uses in the file.c translation unit. ext4_dio_read_iter and ext4_dio_write_iter return -EAGAIN for this result at fs/ext4/file.c:75 and fs/ext4/file.c:520.
A busy inode causes shared lock acquisition to fail for IOCB_NOWAIT; direct write returns -EAGAIN before proceeding.
Exclusive trylock can lose to another holder on IOCB_NOWAIT; direct write returns -EAGAIN.
VFS privilege or timestamp update can fail before direct write; the error exit releases whichever inode lock was taken.
The orphan-list state determines whether successful extending write needs orphan cleanup.
Generic write limits and swapfile checks can return a negative errno; ext4 propagates it before writing.
The header's inode lock-state query only supplies a WARN_ON_ONCE for the size update precondition.
VFS privilege or timestamp update failure is returned before submitting the buffered write.
The task-state query can observe a pending fatal signal; ext4 maps that existing condition to EINTR, and the query itself does not fail.
Allocating the fsmap record with GFP_NOFS can fail; record assembly returns -ENOMEM.
File data writeback or its wait can fail; ext4_sync_file takes the out path before journal synchronization.
The no-journal buffer fsync can return data or metadata writeback failure; ext4 avoids parent sync on error and returns the status.
The helper predicts whether the journal will issue a data barrier; absence makes ext4 request an explicit flush.
An inode with no dcache alias is an expected lookup miss; this parent-walk helper returns success without walking.
Associated buffer writeback can report -EIO; ext4 breaks the parent walk, drops its dentry reference and returns the error.
Synchronous inode metadata writeback can fail; ext4 stops the parent walk, drops its reference and returns the error.
The inode free path does not check or propagate the quota initialization result and continues to dquot_free_inode.
The test-and-clear primitive returns the previous inode bitmap bit. An already clear bit changes the cleanup path but is not a failure of the primitive.

The call uses __GFP_NOFAIL through include/linux/buffer_head.h:378. This path rejects out-of-range bitmap blocks at fs/ext4/ialloc.c:136, and mount validates device size at fs/ext4/super.c:4746. The NULL branch is defensive for the validated geometry.
A cached buffer with BH_Uptodate skips the normal inode bitmap submission path.
The synchronous inode-bitmap read can fail and leave BH_Uptodate clear. This check drops the buffer reference, reports the I/O failure, marks the inode bitmap corrupt and returns ERR_PTR(-EIO).
The group-lock wrapper handles contention by raising the counter and acquiring the lock via the blocking path.
Tests whether the inode bit was already set; that ordinary state returns success without marking the inode again.
Allocating the new VFS inode can return NULL. Inode creation immediately terminates with -ENOMEM before using EXT4_I.

With FS_ENCRYPTION off the stub still returns -EOPNOTSUPP for an already encrypted parent (include/linux/fscrypt.h:636). The ext4 lookup fallback allows the creation check to reach this call and the caller discards the new inode on error.
Active quota record acquisition can fail. The new inode has not yet started normal allocation, so the caller drops it via out and returns the quota error.
The operation returns the old inode bitmap bit; if another allocator set it first, the caller searches again while holding the group lock.
The VFS hash insertion can return -EBUSY when an inode with this identity is already present. The caller reports possible duplicate allocation, marks the inode bitmap corrupt, and returns -EIO.
Quota accounting can reject the new inode with -EDQUOT. The caller takes fail_drop to release the allocated inode state.
The FS_ENCRYPTION-disabled prepare stub never sets the local encrypt flag initialized to false. The guarded set_context call is unreachable in this build.
Looking up the parent's default ACL can return ERR_PTR for xattr I/O or allocation failure. The credit estimator returns PTR_ERR instead of estimating from a bad ACL.
Tests the handle and journal abort state to avoid recording fsync transaction IDs for an already aborted handle. The query itself has no failure result.
Reads one inode allocation bit. A clear bit causes bad-orphan validation, but the bit read itself cannot fail.
Reads the allocation bit only to print its value after bad-orphan handling has already started.
The block zeroing operation can fail with a block-layer I/O error. The inode table initializer jumps to its error exit without marking the group initialized.
Samples BH_Uptodate as one component of the cached bitmap validity predicate. The result is a state bit.
Uses the cached verification bit to skip inode bitmap validation when it was already verified.
Rechecks the cached verification bit under the group lock; a false result requests normal checksum verification.
This is a buffer cache lookup without allocation or I/O. A miss is treated as no recent cached deletion and the caller does not report an error.
Checks cached inode table contents before looking at deletion time. A buffer without BH_Uptodate is skipped as a normal cache state.
A dirty buffer selects a longer recent-deletion window. The flag read has no error outcome.
An invalid on-disk indirect block address can reach and fail the live device bounds check in fs/buffer.c:1084 despite __GFP_NOFAIL. This caller sets -ENOMEM and stops traversing the branch.
False from bh_uptodate_or_lock means a locked buffer needs to be read. The separate ext4_read_bh call performs I/O and is responsible for any read failure.
Uses a block allocated by ext4 in the same branch construction. sb_getblk uses __GFP_NOFAIL for that valid block; the -ENOMEM branch is defensive.

When journaling is active, successful write-access preparation should leave a journal head attached. If it was unexpectedly detached during block clearing, the caller reports filesystem corruption and skips dirtying the invalid buffer.
The GFP_NOFS temporary copy of inline data can fail to allocate. The caller records -ENOMEM and takes the cleanup exit before conversion.
The inline conversion requests a valid mapped data block. sb_getblk uses __GFP_NOFAIL, so valid-block buffer allocation cannot take the -ENOMEM restore branch.
The inline-directory scratch buffer can fail allocation. The caller unlocks xattr_sem and returns -ENOMEM instead of building the tree.
The GFP_NOFS directory copy can fail allocation. The caller releases xattr_sem and returns -ENOMEM rather than iterating the entries.
The symlink payload allocation can fail. The caller takes the cleanup exit with ret already set to -ENOMEM.
Allocation for the shortened inline xattr can fail for its nonzero value length. The caller records -ENOMEM and enters the truncate error cleanup.
Zero-filled allocation for the new inline xattr value can fail. The caller sets -ENOMEM and leaves through out.
The kzalloc wrapper forwards its caller's fail-capable GFP_NOFS allocation to kmalloc and returns NULL unchanged; ext4_update_inline_data checks it and exits with -ENOMEM.
The lock-state query only feeds WARN_ON_ONCE for a regular inode; it does not acquire the lock or return an operation error.
Quota initialization can fail, but inode eviction ignores its result and continues deletion and cleanup.
Checks writeback list membership to see whether the evicting inode needs to be removed before deletion.
List emptiness is used only by the post-eviction invariant warning.
The fast-commit list membership determines whether to disable fast commit while clearing the inode. Reading the list sentinel cannot fail.
Only warns if an established inode is truncated without the expected lock. The state accessor cannot fail.
Block zeroing can return negative I/O status. This wrapper passes it up unchanged after normalizing only positive returns.
Checks unwritten-extent state to mark an existing buffer as new before zeroing; the checked operation status is the separate ret value.
The buffer is for a mapped physical block returned by ext4_map_blocks. sb_getblk allocates with __GFP_NOFAIL; the valid mapping does not yield a normal allocation failure.
A newly mapped buffer without BH_Uptodate is zeroed before use. This is normal buffer initialization.
A set BH_Write_EIO records an actual failed write. The helper restores BH_Uptodate so the callers preserve the newer cached data and avoid replacing it with older disk contents.
Returns the buffer's uptodate flag after write error handling has adjusted it. This is a state read.
After waiting for the batch reads, a non-hole buffer with BH_Uptodate clear denotes a failed read. The caller releases the batch, clears its buffer pointers, and returns -EIO.
Checks whether wait_on_buffer needs to sleep. An unlocked buffer is a normal outcome and the flag read cannot fail.
The buffer flag indicates whether a position outside the requested segment should set the partial marker, without submitting any I/O.
Unmapped buffers are skipped successfully because they do not require journal write access.
The freed flag identifies an obsolete buffer and causes an ordinary successful skip of journal write access.
The path clears a stale BH_New marker before checking mapping. The bit read does not fail.
An unmapped buffer triggers the separate get_block operation. Mapping state itself is not an error return.
After successful mapping the new-buffer flag selects journal access and zeroing setup.
An uncached partial block may need an ordinary preparatory read. Testing BH_Uptodate only decides whether to submit it.
A delayed-allocation flag suppresses a read of a block without committed backing. The getter reports mapping lifecycle state.
An unwritten flag selects normal partial-write handling without reading existing block data. This is buffer state.
After the partial-block read has completed, a clear BH_Uptodate records failure. The write preparation records -EIO, zeroes new buffers through its error path, and returns the error.
The call is gated by fscrypt_inode_uses_fs_layer_crypto, which is false in this build because the disabled fscrypt_needs_contents_encryption always returns false (include/linux/fscrypt.h:458).
The bit test selects new buffers intersecting the unwritten part of the journalled write for zeroing.
An unwritten delayed-write mapping needs BH_New and BH_Mapped set. The flag reader has no failure result.
Reads inode size to detect an overwrite for which existing blocks can be used. It imposes an ordinary size boundary.
Reads file size to see whether the hole punch overlaps EOF, which determines whether on-disk size needs updating.
The lock-state check only triggers WARN_ON if the caller's locking precondition is not met.
This inline instance reads inode lock state for the same regular-inode warning before updating i_disksize.
With DAX disabled the helper returns NULL; even with DAX enabled this means that no pinned page needs waiting and the caller returns success.
VFS privilege removal or timestamp updates can fail in file_modified. Hole punching then releases its locks and returns the error before removing blocks.
jbd2_alloc_inode is a GFP_KERNEL slab allocation. NULL returns -ENOMEM if another thread has not already installed a journal inode.
This inline transaction ID update skips an already aborted handle; the predicate itself does not produce a new failure.
The inode table and offset come from mount-validated group geometry (fs/ext4/super.c:3347). sb_getblk cannot fail allocation for that valid block because it uses __GFP_NOFAIL.
sb_getblk uses __GFP_NOFAIL for the validated bitmap block. The NULL check only disables an optimization and continues with the normal inode table read.
If the bitmap is not already cached and uptodate, the caller drops its reference and takes the ordinary inode-table read path.
Reading an inode allocation bit identifies another live inode and thus the need to read the shared inode-table block.

This check runs after the inode-table read completes. A failed read leaves BH_Uptodate clear. The caller records the block when requested, releases its buffer, and returns -EIO to the inode lookup path.
The VFS inode lookup allocates a new inode on a cache miss and may return NULL. ext4 converts that to ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM).
This reads i_size just set from disk. A negative value is corrupt metadata and is reported by ext4's validation, not a failure of the size accessor.
BH_Req indicates whether a request occurred; it merely gates interpretation of the companion uptodate bit after writeback.

In no-journal inode writeback, the preceding BH_Req check establishes that I/O was requested. A clear BH_Uptodate identifies failed I/O here, so ext4 reports the inode-table writeback error and returns -EIO.
The VFS setattr permission or size checks can reject the change with a negative errno. ext4 returns it before updating inode attributes.
A path-based attribute change can reach an inode carrying S_ENCRYPTED. Without FS_ENCRYPTION the underlying setattr stub returns -EOPNOTSUPP and ext4 propagates it.
ext4 loads S_VERITY from on-disk flags even without FS_VERITY. For such an inode, the setattr stub returns -EOPNOTSUPP and ext4 propagates it.
Preparing quota records before an ownership or size change can fail for active quotas. ext4 returns the error before starting the update.
Moving an inode's quota charge can fail on quota limits or quota record acquisition. ext4 releases xattr_sem, stops the handle, and returns before applying the inode IDs.
A journal flush can fail on journal abort or checkpoint I/O. ext4 unlocks journal updates, releases its writepages exclusion, and propagates the error.
Reads inode size after locking the folio to detect a concurrent truncate. The size report itself cannot fail.
Rechecks size on the journalled write-fault path so a truncated folio is not used. The no-page result reflects a normal race.
Reads an approximate free-cluster count to decide whether delayed allocation should be avoided.
Reads the dirty-cluster estimate to compare it with free space and decide when to push delayed-allocation writeback.
Negates BH_Mapped to answer the page-walk callback's mapping question. No mapping operation is attempted.
The write completion callback skips an unmapped buffer and returns success; the flag reader cannot fail.
The write completion callback skips a freed buffer without dirtying it. The flag reports buffer lifecycle state.
Block quota reservation can return -EDQUOT when allocation exceeds an active limit. ext4 propagates it before updating its own reservation accounting.
Reads inode size to clamp the persisted end of the mapped extent. No error value is returned by the size read.
Reads inode size to trim the submitted folio length at EOF. Any write error comes from the later submission.
Reads inode size to cap the amount of folio data passed to the journal near EOF.
Converts inode size to a logical block boundary for iterating page buffers.
Only asserts that buffers must be unlocked when iterated. BH_Lock is a state bit and there is no recovery action.
A clean buffer needs no mapping for writeback. The bit chooses whether to continue normal extent accumulation.
An unmapped buffer is excluded from this writeback extent by ordinary mapping-state logic.
The delayed-allocation flag selects buffers that still need mapping for writeback.
The unwritten flag selects buffers needing unwritten-extent conversion as part of regular writeback.
Detects a delayed buffer so the caller can assign the resolved physical block and clear BH_Delay.
File size separates allocation past EOF from the in-file extent creation path. This is ordinary size-based routing.
Reads inode size to decide whether an iomap past EOF must carry IOMAP_F_DIRTY.
Queries whether the data-sync transaction has committed to decide whether the inode is still dirty; not committed is a normal journal state.
Fast-commit list membership supplies the inode's data-sync dirty classification.
The mapping's private list indicates pending metadata buffers. Empty and nonempty are both ordinary state.
The journal bit is tested only by a warning in the non-journalled data invalidation path.
A currently unmapped end buffer indicates that i_disksize should not yet be advanced.
Delayed allocation at the end of the write indicates the recorded on-disk size must not be advanced yet.
An unwritten end buffer is a normal reason to defer the i_disksize update.
The freed bit causes the zeroing helper to skip a buffer already released by the journal.
Tests whether block lookup is required before zeroing a buffer. The mapping flag carries no errno.
After lookup the unmapped flag is treated as a hole and zeroing is skipped. It does not carry the separate lookup status.
A buffer that lacks BH_Uptodate needs to be read. ext4_read_bh_lock is the operation whose return can report an I/O error.
Disabled fscrypt_needs_contents_encryption returns false, so the guarded decryption call and its error branch are unreachable (include/linux/fscrypt.h:458).
Converts the in-memory project ID to its on-disk numeric value in the initial namespace. The later -EFSCORRUPTED guard checks the project feature and ID rather than a conversion failure.
The orphan-list state selects whether to clear the legacy high UID/GID fields for a deleted inode.
The RCU lookup only visits other inodes already cached. A miss skips the opportunistic timestamp update without an error.
Freezing the block device can fail in the holder callback or synchronous writeback. The default shutdown path propagates that failure before setting the shutdown flag.
Reads whether the journal has already been aborted before deciding whether to request a final commit and abort.
Skips a second journal abort in the no-log-flush path. Reading the abort flag is not itself a failure.
Writeback or its recorded completion can report an I/O error. The immutable-flag update branches to flags_out before installing the new flag.
Quota record initialization can fail for an active quota. The project-ID ioctl returns the error before accessing and updating the inode record.
Mount write access can fail with -EROFS. The version-setting ioctl returns immediately before accepting the new generation.
A read-only mount rejects the write request. The group-extend ioctl takes its resize cleanup exit with the error.
Journal flush can fail on an aborted journal or checkpoint I/O. The group-extend ioctl unlocks updates and returns the flush error when extension itself succeeded.
Failure to copy the move-extent request from userspace returns a positive uncopied count; the ioctl reports -EFAULT before using the donor fd.
Mount write access can return -EROFS even after the file was opened for writing. The extent-move ioctl releases the donor fd at mext_out and returns the error.
Copying the extent-move result back to userspace can be incomplete. The ioctl sets -EFAULT, drops the donor fd, and returns the error.
An inaccessible group-add input buffer makes the copy incomplete. The ioctl returns -EFAULT without starting the group addition.
A read-only mount rejects write permission for migration. The ioctl propagates the error before taking the inode lock or migrating the mapping.
Mount write authorization can return -EROFS. The force-allocation ioctl returns before allocating delayed blocks.
The mount can become read-only even with a write-mode file. This ioctl returns the write-access error before swapping the boot-loader inode.
A short userspace size copy returns an uncopied byte count. The resize ioctl maps it to -EFAULT before beginning resize.
The resize ioctl must acquire mount write access, and a read-only mount returns -EROFS. It uses resizefs_out to end the resize attempt on failure.
An aborted journal or failed checkpoint can make this flush return an error. The resize ioctl unlocks journal updates and propagates it if resizing otherwise succeeded.
The helper reads the device queue's discard limit. Zero means no discard support and the ioctl rejects the operation, but the capability query cannot fail.
The input trim range can be inaccessible to copy_from_user. The FITRIM ioctl returns -EFAULT before starting trimming.
The trimmed-range result may not fit in an accessible userspace buffer. An incomplete copy returns -EFAULT to the ioctl caller.
Group addition requires mount write access, which can return -EROFS. The helper takes group_add_out to finish the resize attempt and propagate the error.
The post-addition journal flush can return checkpoint or journal abort errors. The helper releases the journal lock and preserves the flush error when adding the group succeeded.
The fsmap header read can be incomplete if userspace memory is inaccessible. The ioctl returns -EFAULT before validating fields.
Searches the reserved header bytes for a nonzero value. -EINVAL describes invalid input contents, not a failure of the memory search.
Validates the low key's reserved bytes via a pure memory search. Finding a byte differs from the specified value is ordinary output.
The pure memory search validates the high key's reserved bytes; it does not return a failure of its own.
Writing the last-record flag into the userspace fsmap array can be incomplete. The ioctl returns -EFAULT immediately.
A partial copy of the updated fsmap header back to userspace makes the ioctl return -EFAULT instead of success.
Writing back the file mapping can report I/O or writeback setup failure. The inode swap exits through err_out before modifying the mappings.
Writing back the boot-loader inode mapping can report an I/O error independently of the ordinary file. The swap takes err_out and leaves inode data unchanged.
Initializing the file's active quotas can fail. The caller takes err_out1 to stop the journal transaction and unwind before swapping data.
Quota charging for the changed block count can return -EDQUOT; the caller reverts the inode data and accounting changes on negative errno.
Copying the fiemap request from userspace can leave bytes uncopied; the caller returns -EFAULT before enumerating cached extents.
Copying the updated fiemap header back can be short; the caller changes the ioctl result to -EFAULT.
An inaccessible checkpoint flag pointer leaves bytes uncopied; the ioctl exits with -EFAULT before checking flags or flushing.
Returns the queue discard limit. Zero means the device lacks discard capability; the caller rejects the requested mode with -EOPNOTSUPP, but the limit query cannot fail.
Controls whether the zeroout warning is emitted; suppression does not change the journal flush.
Journal flush can encounter checkpoint errors or an aborted journal (fs/jbd2/journal.c:2427). The ioctl unlocks updates and returns the flush status directly.
The volume-label destination may not be writable; the ioctl returns -EFAULT if the copy leaves bytes uncopied.
Copying the new volume-label bytes from userspace can fault before label validation; nonzero remainder is returned as -EFAULT.
The mount can reject write access with -EROFS (fs/namespace.c:531); the ioctl propagates it before changing the label.
The userspace UUID request header may be inaccessible; a short copy becomes -EFAULT.
The caller writes the required size on a length-query request; an unwritable length field returns -EFAULT.
The first UUID output copy writes the header; a short copy immediately causes -EFAULT.
The second UUID output copy writes the UUID bytes; header success does not guarantee payload accessibility and a short copy returns -EFAULT.
The UUID setter copies and validates the request header; an inaccessible source returns -EFAULT before validation.
Even after copying the UUID header, payload bytes may be inaccessible; the setter returns -EFAULT on incomplete payload copy.
The UUID setter propagates mount write refusal such as -EROFS before updating superblocks.
Writing a mapping record to its userspace destination may be short; the formatter returns -EFAULT to the fsmap walk.

The primary superblock buffer records a previous failed write in BH_Write_EIO. This result enters explicit recovery that logs the old error and resets both buffer flags before writing the updated superblock.

A failed write can leave BH_Uptodate clear with BH_Write_EIO set. This second condition normally short-circuits, but a concurrent recovery clears BH_Write_EIO before setting BH_Uptodate (for example, fs/ext4/super.c:6182-6183), allowing this check to detect and repair that transient state.
Tests readiness of a successfully obtained prefetch buffer to update a counter; data can simply still be in flight.
Both slab and vmalloc backing may fail for the buddy group pointer table; NULL is reported and returned as -ENOMEM.
GFP_NOFS slab allocation of the group record can fail; the caller checks the stored pointer, unwinds the new metadata table when needed, and returns -ENOMEM.
The initial average-fragment list array may fail to allocate; NULL sets -ENOMEM and enters shared cleanup.
Allocation of average-fragment locks may fail after the list array succeeded; the common -ENOMEM path frees the allocated arrays.
Failure allocating the largest-free-order list array sets -ENOMEM and frees existing average-fragment arrays.
Failure allocating the largest-free-order lock array sets -ENOMEM and frees the existing lists and locks.
Per-CPU locality-group allocation can return NULL on resource exhaustion; initialization frees the earlier arrays and returns -ENOMEM.
Creating the group-info slab cache without SLAB_PANIC can fail under memory pressure; NULL is logged and returned as -ENOMEM.
Creating the buddy-cache inode can fail during inode allocation; caller logs it, frees group information, and returns -ENOMEM.
Checks the discard queue is drained after flush_work; nonempty is an invariant warning, not an error from the list query.
A busy group spinlock is expected; the caller updates contention accounting and acquires the lock with spin_lock.
Tests whether the discard queue is empty before appending; this chooses whether to enqueue the worker.
An empty input list requires no tail splice; the list query does no allocation or I/O.
WARN_RATELIMIT uses the limiter only to choose whether to issue a warning. The bitmap folio mapping mismatch independently controls the -EINVAL branch.
The buddy folio mapping mismatch independently causes -EINVAL; the limiter only decides whether the diagnostic is printed.
GFP_NOFS allocation of the block-allocation context can fail; the caller clears the returned length, sets *errp to -ENOMEM, and exits.
NULL means no adjacent preallocation node lies to the left; the caller switches search paths for this ordinary tree boundary.
The predecessor iterator ends when there is no remaining nondeleted left candidate; the caller tries group preallocation.
The preallocation descriptor slab can run out of memory at GFP_NOFS; NULL is returned to the caller as -ENOMEM.
The underlying buddy-load status controls the early return; the limiter only suppresses or emits its warning.
This free-path descriptor allocation explicitly uses GFP_NOFS with __GFP_NOFAIL, and the caller relies on success without a NULL branch.
Reads the spinlock state only for the group-lock assertion before freeing buddy blocks.
The temporary array of bitmap buffer pointers can fail allocation on a GFP_NOFS path (mballoc.c:1733); NULL immediately returns -ENOMEM.

This check runs after waiting for and validating each bitmap. A failed bitmap read or validation can leave BH_Verified clear. The caller skips the faulty bitmap and uses only verified bitmaps to initialize the buddy cache.
An empty list needs no splice or reinitialization; the header helper tests list structure.
Checks group-lock ownership as an assertion before trimming; the query does not fail.
Reads group-lock held state for an assertion before marking buddy blocks used; it does not request a lock.
The predecessor lookup can legitimately find no left neighbor; the overlap algorithm then keeps only the right preallocation neighbor.
The overlap walk stops at the end of the left-neighbor chain; NULL is normal tree traversal.
The missing buddy condition controls skipping the group; the ratelimit result only controls printing the warning.
Reads group-lock state for the assertion that protects the buddy search.
Quickly skips a largest-free-order bucket with no groups before taking the bucket read lock.
Rechecks the bucket under its read lock; a now-empty bucket is unlocked and skipped as normal concurrent state.
An empty average-fragment bucket means there is no group suggestion; the unlocked preliminary search returns NULL.
The locked recheck may find an empty bucket; returning no suggestion after unlocking is an ordinary search result.
An empty group preallocation list means there is nothing to discard. The bitmap read with its own error handling is later.
NULL merely means the inserted extent has no left neighbor eligible for merge.

MMP validates the block against filesystem geometry before the initial lookup and keeps the buffer for subsequent reads. The no-fail lookup cannot return NULL within validated committed geometry. The separate read at mmp.c:97 can still return an I/O error.
This check reads the completion result of the MMP block write submitted at mmp.c:51. The write completion clears BH_Uptodate on device I/O failure and the caller returns -EIO.
A differing node name can indicate a genuine multiply mounted filesystem, but memcmp only compares the stored bytes and cannot fail.
Reads the folio's optional private buffer pointer; if no buffers are attached, the ordinary setup path creates them.
Missing private buffers are an expected folio state; the caller creates empty buffers before reading.
Checks whether an out-of-range buffer is already current and records partial coverage; no failure has occurred.
An already-current buffer needs no work; a noncurrent one enters the ordinary mapping and read path.
The first mapping query tests whether a block lookup is needed; errors from that lookup are checked separately.
An unmapped buffer following successful block lookup represents a hole, so the range is zero-filled.
Rechecks validity after acquiring the buffer lock to avoid duplicate I/O; noncurrent data is read normally.

For a requested mapped buffer that needed a read, this check runs after the caller waits for completion. A failed read leaves BH_Uptodate clear and the caller returns -EIO from the extent move preparation.
Reports pending fatal-signal state. The directory walk handles cancellation with -ERESTARTSYS, but this is a task-state query.
In this configuration ext4_readdir returns the encryption stub's -EOPNOTSUPP at dir.c:138 before entering the htree walk for an encrypted directory.
This allocation stub is unreachable: the caller path already rejects encrypted enumeration at dir.c:138, and even this helper exits on fscrypt_prepare_readdir before reaching it.
This disk-name conversion stub is reachable only through the encrypted htree branch, but fscrypt_prepare_readdir rejects that directory before any conversion (dir.c:138 and namei.c:1095).
Compares the first directory name with the literal dot; mismatching disk data triggers the warning, not a comparison failure.
Compares the second directory name with dot-dot; the return encodes equality even when ext4 warns about malformed data.
A verified directory block bypasses the checksum work. Unverified status is not itself a checksum error.
The no-encryption stub always returns false (include/linux/fscrypt.h:562). -EPERM rejects an encrypted directory context as policy; the predicate does not fail.
Quota initialization for the parent directory can fail when loading an active dquot; file creation propagates the error before allocating an inode.
An existing encrypted parent can reach the no-encryption link stub and get -EOPNOTSUPP; ext4 returns that failure before increasing link count.
Quota initialization may fail loading the hard-link target directory's quota state; error is returned before starting the link update.
A quota-load failure for the containing directory takes out_trace and returns its errno without attempting unlink.
A quota-load failure for the inode being removed takes out_trace before the namespace change; directory quota success does not initialize the target inode's distinct quota state.
The no-encryption wrapper can reject an existing encrypted parent with -EOPNOTSUPP and can reject an oversized symlink with -ENAMETOOLONG; both statuses are returned.
A parent-directory dquot lookup can fail after the symlink parameters are prepared; the caller propagates the failure without creating the inode.
This build rejects encrypted-parent symlink creation at namei.c:3375. The new inode on the remaining path is unencrypted, so the encryption-error cleanup is unreachable here.
Loading the parent dquot can fail; mkdir returns the quota error before beginning its creation transaction.
Quota initialization for the parent directory can fail before rmdir looks up the child; the function returns the error immediately.
Initialization for the child directory's quota state can fail separately and rmdir returns before removing its entry.
Parent quota initialization may return an error while loading quota state; mknod stops before inode creation.
A rename involving an existing encrypted directory can reach the no-encryption stub and return -EOPNOTSUPP before rename/exchange starts.
Quota initialization of the temporary file's containing directory can fail; tmpfile returns that error before inode allocation.
The no-encryption name matcher compares bytes of equal-length names; a difference is ordinary lookup behavior.

This check runs after waiting for the buffered directory read. A failed read leaves BH_Uptodate clear, so the caller reports the I/O error, releases the buffer and returns ERR_PTR(-EIO) through cleanup.
The unverified flag enables validation; the separate failing checksum comparison, not the flag read, causes -EFSBADCRC.
Checks the first dx root directory name against dot. A mismatch proves malformed metadata but does not mean strncmp failed.
Checks the parent dx root name against dot-dot. The comparison reports a value for malformed as well as valid input.
During exchange rename, failure loading quota for the source directory stops the operation and is returned before entry lookup.
The exchange target directory may need its own dquot load; failure is returned before the exchange transaction.
Rename aborts before entry lookup if initializing the source directory's active dquot fails.
A dquot load for the source inode can fail separately from its directory; rename propagates the result.
A dquot load for the target directory can fail; rename propagates it before changing namespace state.
When replacing an existing inode, a failure loading its quota state is returned before any rename changes are made.
Compares the directory's first on-disk name with dot. Corruption handling belongs to the name validator, not to the string comparison.
Compares the directory's second on-disk name with dot-dot; the caller reports corrupt metadata on mismatch.
A name mismatch means the cached entry cannot be reused; the caller finds it again before deletion.
Tests whether the inode lock is held for an orphan-add invariant warning; no lock operation takes place.
A nonempty inode orphan link means it is already tracked, so adding it is idempotent.

A negative result means this block has no available orphan slots, so the search checks other blocks. Only exhaustion of the whole orphan file produces -ENOSPC and triggers fallback to the legacy orphan list.
Tests inode-lock state for a warning in orphan removal; it does not acquire a lock.
An inode absent from the legacy orphan list needs no removal; the helper returns success.
Reads the block device's read-only state to skip cleanup on write-protected media; the state query cannot fail.
An active quota lookup may fail, but orphan processing discards dquot_initialize's return and continues with truncation or inode removal.
GFP_KERNEL allocation for orphan-block metadata can fail; caller sets -ENOMEM and drops its inode reference.
The I/O completion vector allocation has no no-fail flag; NULL is returned as ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) before linking the vector.
Test is only the nonempty-list assertion before obtaining the last vector.
The unwritten completion queue can simply be drained; list emptiness exits the loop normally.
The I/O completion object allocation may fail with the callers' GFP_KERNEL flags; NULL propagates to writepages, which turns it into -ENOMEM (fs/ext4/inode.c:2672 and 2689).
An empty completion vector list means there is no unwritten extent conversion to schedule; the caller releases the object.
Checks that an object being released is no longer queued; nonempty is a BUG_ON invariant rather than an allocation or I/O failure.
The conversion list being empty means the caller must schedule its worker before queuing the first object.
A clean buffer is ineligible for this writeback pass; its dirty-state check cannot fail.
Delayed allocation means the buffer is not ready for this writeback path; the flag selects ordinary deferral.
An unmapped buffer is excluded from this submission pass, for example when it covers a hole.
The unwritten extent flag is normal mapping state and selects the deferred writeback path.
The second mapped-state check detects a hole so its dirty bit can safely be cleared.
Checks whether the skipped buffer still needs writeback; dirty state keeps the folio on the to-write list.
Tests journal ownership before reading journal dirty state; this is a buffer state query.
The journal dirty flag indicates pending journaled data and can keep a skipped folio dirty; the accessor reports ordinary state.
Checks whether a new-buffer bit should be cleared before marking the buffer for async write.
CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION is disabled, so the writeback encryption branch is unreachable. If compiled with encryption, the limiter would only control the diagnostic.
CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION is disabled, so the writeback encryption branch is unreachable. The async-write flag is only a state query used to select which buffers to redirty in that branch.
The async-write flag selects buffers prepared for submission; unset is an ordinary skipped-buffer state.
Counts outstanding buffers outside the completed BIO range; it queries state and does not report the BIO status.
No completion vectors means the free loop has nothing to release.
A prior I/O failure caused this diagnostic helper to run; the limiter only decides whether the error is printed.
Folio private buffers select the fallback read implementation; this is ordinary optional attachment state.
bio_alloc can fail for some flags, but GFP_KERNEL permits direct reclaim and allocation from fs_bio_set has the documented guarantee (block/bio.c:503). This caller assumes success.
The slab mempool and its initial reserves can fail to allocate; the caller destroys the slab cache and returns -ENOMEM.
Failure allocating an RCU callback node switches from deferred freeing to synchronize_rcu followed by kvfree.
The new group-data array can fail to allocate with GFP_NOFS; the code frees flex_gd and returns NULL to the resize caller.
The group-flags array can fail allocation after group-data allocation; cleanup frees both the data array and flex descriptor before returning NULL.

A pending online grow uses a previously checked device capacity. If capacity retracts before the first lookup of a new descriptor block, the live bounds check in fs/buffer.c:1084 can reject it despite __GFP_NOFAIL. The caller exits setup with -ENOMEM.
Zeroing reserved backup descriptor blocks can fail in the block layer; the function follows its resize cleanup path and propagates the status.
Zeroing the new group's inode table can fail with a block I/O error; the resize transaction leaves via out and reports the failure.

If capacity retracts during online grow and a new backup block is absent from cache, the live bounds check in fs/buffer.c:1084 can reject it despite __GFP_NOFAIL. The caller ends backup updates and clears EXT4_VALID_FS to request a filesystem check.

The live capacity check in fs/buffer.c:1084 can reject an uncached new bitmap or group descriptor if capacity retracts during online grow. The helper returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) and its caller unwinds setup.

The earlier setup drops its buffer reference. With no journal pin, writeback and reclaim can leave a cache miss. A capacity retraction during online grow can then make the live bounds check in fs/buffer.c:1084 reject the lookup, and the caller returns -ENOMEM.
GFP_NOFS allocation of the backup descriptor array may return NULL; the resize helper returns -ENOMEM.
The GFP_KERNEL allocation of the expanded meta block group descriptor table can fail; the caller releases gdb_bh and returns -ENOMEM.
Allocating the expanded descriptor table can fail; add_new_gdb logs allocation failure and unwinds through its -ENOMEM error path.

The initial setup can skip an uninitialized inode bitmap, so checksum setup can need its first lookup. If capacity retracts during online grow, the live bounds check in fs/buffer.c:1084 can reject the new block despite __GFP_NOFAIL. The resize caller converts NULL to -EIO.
False means the buffer is not yet uptodate and was locked by the helper; ext4 then submits a read whose own status reports any I/O failure.
The lock bit is read to assert the precondition for submitting an asynchronous read; the accessor has no failure result.
BH_Write_EIO records a failed write. The read helper restores BH_Uptodate so that reading the old disk contents cannot replace the newer cached data.
The accessor returns the cached buffer's readiness after ext4 accounts for a prior write error; it cannot fail itself.
The lock bit is read solely for BUG_ON enforcing the synchronous read helper's buffer locking precondition.
After the read is submitted and the buffer is unlocked by completion, a clear BH_Uptodate reports a failed read and ext4_read_bh returns -EIO.
The lock bit only decides whether wait_on_buffer must wait for the owner; neither outcome is a failure of the query.
Ordinary contention on the nonblocking buffer lock leads to the blocking lock operation; the higher level operation does not fail.
The buffer acquisition may return NULL; the caller returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) before attempting the superblock read.
If the buffer lock is contended the optional readahead is skipped and the reference is released; there is no reported operation failure.
The rate limiter only gates printing of this existing ext4 error; it has no error return of its own.
Read-only is a device property; this branch controls whether ext4 can persist information for an already detected error.
The rate limiter determines whether the existing inode error is printed; suppression is expected and cannot fail the inode operation.
The rate limiter controls optional pathname lookup and printing while reporting an existing file error.
Reading current->journal_info may report that no transaction is active; this suppresses logging of a previously received -EROFS on a read-only mount.
The rate limiter gates decoding and logging the error supplied by the caller; a suppressed message is not a failing operation.
A suppressed informational message is the expected result of rate limiting; the caller simply returns from logging.
The warning wrapper returns the limiter's print/no-print decision; this is not an error status.
Rate limiting governs the group-specific diagnostic for an already detected error and does not fail the group operation.
The read-only property determines whether error metadata may be queued for persistence; the check itself cannot fail.
On spinlock contention the caller updates its contention counter and takes the blocking lock; the operation does not report failure.
The test-and-set returns the previous block-bitmap corruption flag so the free-cluster count is corrected once; it does not discover or cause the corruption.
The previous inode-bitmap corruption flag determines whether free-inode accounting must be adjusted; the bit operation itself cannot fail.
The GFP_KERNEL allocation of the flex-group pointer table may fail; ext4 logs the failure and returns -ENOMEM.
The per-flex-group allocation may fail; the caller frees the newly allocated groups and pointer table before returning -ENOMEM.
Allocation of the lazy initialization request can fail; NULL is returned to ext4_register_li_request which propagates -ENOMEM.
Allocation of the lazy initialization controller can fail; this routine returns -ENOMEM before initializing the request list.
A GFP_NOFS zeroed page can be unavailable; the overhead computation returns -ENOMEM before using its scratch buffer.

Under this built-in configuration ext4 registers its unique static type once and filesystem parameter validation is disabled. The rollback guards registration errors exposed by the general API but not expected here.

discard_buffer() clears BH_Mapped and would make ext4_commit_super() return -EIO (fs/buffer.c:1573-1589, fs/ext4/super.c:6165-6170). The normal block-size change path cannot do this to ext4's retained superblock buffer: ext4 releases it before sb_set_blocksize() calls kill_bdev() (fs/ext4/super.c:5054-5061), while get_tree_bdev() claims the block device for the mounted filesystem and BLKBSZSET must obtain an exclusive open (fs/super.c:1552-1554, block/ioctl.c:540-546). No supported path was found that discards this buffer while the filesystem is mounted.
BH_Write_EIO reports an earlier failed superblock write. The error branch logs it, restores the cached buffer state and submits a new write.

A failed write can leave BH_Uptodate clear with BH_Write_EIO set. This second condition normally short-circuits, but a concurrent updater can clear BH_Write_EIO before setting BH_Uptodate (fs/ext4/ioctl.c:81-82 or fs/ext4/super.c:780-781), allowing this check to detect and repair that transient state.
The write completion handler records a failed superblock write in BH_Write_EIO. After waiting for completion, ext4 checks it, repairs the flags and returns -EIO.
GFP_KERNEL may fail to allocate the mount context; the initialization returns -ENOMEM without setting fc->fs_private.
Parsing an unknown or invalid mount parameter can return negative errno; ext4_parse_param propagates that error before processing the token.
The journal-device lookup can fail to resolve its path or reject a non-block device; the caller logs the failure and returns -EINVAL.
The search detects a slash in the name and triggers quota name validation; strchr itself only returns match or no match.
The comparison detects conflicting quota names; the caller diagnoses invalid options rather than failure of strcmp.
Allocating the quota name copy can return NULL; the caller logs the memory error and returns -ENOMEM.
The rate limiter controls an informational mount message after mounting; suppression does not fail the mount.
Allocating ext4_sb_info can fail; the helper propagates NULL and the mount path turns it into -ENOMEM.
Allocation of the block-group lock table can fail; the helper goes to err_out to release acquired resources and return NULL.
d_make_root allocates a dentry and consumes the root inode reference even if allocation fails; ext4 reports -ENOMEM and unwinds the mount.
Zero reports that the device does not support discard; ext4 warns about the requested option but the capability query has no error return.
Allocating the on-disk mount-option copy can fail; ret is still -ENOMEM and the mount caller aborts on it.
Failure to allocate the parser context jumps to cleanup for the temporary option string and returns -ENOMEM.
Failure to allocate the private ext4 parse context releases the temporary mount context and option buffer and returns -ENOMEM.
The geometry validator can reject an on-disk block count outside addressable storage; ext4 logs and propagates its negative errno.
The helper reads capacity in filesystem blocks. A mismatch can invalidate the mount geometry but is not a failure of the capacity query.
JBD2 write access can return -EROFS or -EIO after abort or device writeback error; ext4 stops the handle and falls back to writing the superblock directly.
BH_Write_EIO reports a failed prior superblock write. The worker logs the error and restores the buffer state before handing the updated metadata back to JBD2.

A failed write can leave BH_Uptodate clear with BH_Write_EIO set. This second condition normally short-circuits, but ext4_commit_super clears BH_Write_EIO before restoring BH_Uptodate at fs/ext4/super.c:6182-6183; this check can detect and repair that transient state.
An asynchronously aborted JBD2 handle can make dirty_metadata return -EROFS; ext4 stops the transaction and uses the direct-superblock fallback.
The GFP_KERNEL group descriptor array allocation may return NULL; the published NULL is checked and mount initialization returns -ENOMEM.
JBD2 returns whether revoke is supported by the journal format. False normally selects data journalling instead of ordered mode.

This is a boolean capability query: false means the journal format lacks revoke support, not that the query failed (fs/jbd2/journal.c:2241-2265). An explicit ordered/writeback request is consequently rejected as an unsupported configuration; the default-mode query at site 499 falls back to data journaling. Consistent with sites 280 and 298, the capability check itself is not a realistic injected error.
The list emptiness check terminates traversal of commit callbacks; it does not return the transaction error passed separately to those callbacks.
Initialization allocates per-CPU storage for the free-cluster counter; -ENOMEM skips later counter initialization and is propagated.
Per-CPU storage for the free-inode counter can be unavailable; the helper skips subsequent initialization and returns its errno.
Directory counter per-CPU storage allocation may fail; the dirty-cluster and subsequent initialization are skipped and the error is returned.
The dirty-cluster counter allocation can fail; the caller stops initializing per-CPU parameters and returns the status.
Per-CPU storage for the retry-limit counter can fail; the helper skips writepages semaphore initialization and returns the error.
The per-CPU semaphore allocates read counters and may return -ENOMEM; ext4 logs insufficient memory and returns the status.
A flush can return an aborted-journal or checkpoint error; the recovery-completion routine skips clearing recovery state and unlocks the journal before returning it.
Looking for the equals delimiter classifies a mount option as flag or key/value; NULL is a normal search outcome.

Allocating a copy of the option value can fail. parse_options returns -ENOMEM, and the caller logs the failure and discards the on-disk option set rather than applying a partially parsed configuration.
The helper reads whether any quotas are currently loaded; that state is an input to option consistency checks.
The string comparison detects a changed journalled quota file name; the offending option branch does not mean strcmp failed.
The allocation inside the array wrapper may return NULL for the ext4 group descriptor array; the wrapper propagates it to the mount helper's -ENOMEM branch.
GFP_NOFS allocation from the ext4 inode slab can fail; ext4 returns NULL without initializing the inode and the VFS allocation fails.
The orphan list test is an invariant check during inode destruction; the list accessor itself has no failure value.
Testing fast-commit list membership only gates a warning before the inode is freed; the predicate cannot fail.
The VFS drop policy reports whether to evict the inode; a false result allows the encryption-specific drop decision.
The rate limiter controls an unmount message only; suppression does not change unmount cleanup.
The dirty-cluster total is a counter value used for a teardown warning; percpu_counter_sum has no failure return.
The orphan list state only decides whether to dump diagnostic information during unmount; the predicate cannot fail.
The accessor tests a teardown assertion that the orphan list is empty; this is not an operation failure.
The transaction query says whether JBD2 will send a data barrier; a negative answer selects a separate flush rather than reporting an error.
The commit-start result says whether a transaction was selected to commit. ext4 waits when appropriate and errors come from the separate commit wait.
An aborted journal or checkpoint can make jbd2_journal_flush fail; ext4_freeze leaves the recovery flag intact and returns the error after unlocking updates.
The accessor reads current->journal_info; quota writers start a handle first and even no-journal mode installs a non-NULL nesting token. The -EIO branch guards the caller's transaction precondition.
Quota commit can return -EIO for an inactive quota or fail while writing its entry; ext4 reports the error and stops the transaction before returning the status.
Acquiring the quota record can fail on quota file I/O; ext4 reports acquisition failure and stops the transaction while preserving the error.
Writing quota file information can return an I/O error; ext4 stops the handle and preserves that error in preference to the stop status.
Enabling quotas can reject the quota file or fail reading quota metadata; ext4 skips the file-update branch on failure and returns the status.

The quota slot owns the inode reference and is serialized by s_umount; setup stores an igrab reference and cleanup clears the slot before iput. A non-NULL live entry cannot be in the freeing states rejected by igrab.
The journal-device read-only state can prevent a read/write mount; the accessor reports the capability and does not itself perform a failed operation.
The backing-device read-only bit contributes to whether recovery may write to disk; the accessor is a pure property query.
Skipping stale recovery can return a journal scan or I/O error; ext4 skips loading the journal and unwinds the failed mount attempt.
Journal loading can fail when replay or initialization fails; ext4 preserves its status through restoration of saved error metadata and handles the load failure.
The comparison detects whether journal replay changed the ext4 superblock's saved error fields; mismatch is normal data semantics and may trigger restoring those bytes.
A nonzero journal error records an abort or a failure from the previous mount. ext4 marks the filesystem in need of checking and commits that state before clearing the recorded journal error.
Reading the external journal superblock can fail; ext4 reports it and releases the opened device rather than proceeding to journal validation.
Comparing journal UUID bytes can discover a mismatch and reject the journal; the comparison itself has no failure result.
The accessor reads the journal head attached to the buffer and does not create one. The caller redirties only when buffer/transaction state requires it.
The dirty bit is ordinary writeback state; it tells the journalled writepage callback whether to redirty and defer the folio.
dquot_suspend uses the fixed DQUOT_SUSPENDED flag. The only negative return from dquot_disable is for incompatible flag combinations; this invocation cannot reach it (fs/quota/dquot.c:2241).
The predicate reports suspended quota state to choose resume versus enabling quota on the remount; it cannot fail.
The predicate checks whether quota state needs restoring during remount rollback; it does not generate the original error.
An empty lazy initialization work list is normal termination for the worker and does not mean the list check failed.
Contention on s_umount causes the lazy initialization request to be rescheduled; it does not fail the request.
The worker rechecks the pending list under both mutexes to decide whether to resume processing; the check cannot fail.
The inode slab cache can fail to allocate with no SLAB_PANIC flag; init_inodecache returns -ENOMEM and ext4 initialization unwinds.
The ext3 alias is optional and only logs a registration failure. In this configuration the built-in ext4 code owns the ext3 name and registers it once.
The ext2 alias is optional and only logs a registration failure. CONFIG_EXT2_FS is disabled so the ext4 implementation provides the sole built-in ext2 type.
The symlink path uses the helper to retain newer cached data after a failed write recorded in BH_Write_EIO. It restores BH_Uptodate so a reread cannot replace that data with the old disk contents.
Adding the per-superblock kobject can fail to allocate or register its sysfs entry; ext4 puts the kobject and waits for cleanup before returning the error.
Failure to create the per-mount proc directory simply omits optional proc statistics entries; ext4_register_sysfs still succeeds.
Creating and registering the ext4 sysfs root can fail; ext4_init_sysfs returns -ENOMEM without setting up feature entries.
Allocation of the features kobject can fail; ext4 sets -ENOMEM and releases the sysfs root.
Adding the features kobject can fail during sysfs registration; ext4 releases the feature object and root through the error path.
The optional ext4 proc root may be absent while ext4_init_sysfs returns the prior successful sysfs registration status.
A malformed or out-of-range sysfs value makes kstrtoul return errno; the readahead setting is unchanged and the write returns the parse error.
Unsigned parsing for the signed-range attribute can reject malformed input or overflow; the caller returns the parse status before updating the field.
Converting a u32-backed attribute can fail; the caller returns the error before updating the superblock or in-memory value.
Invalid input or overflow in parsing the multiblock order propagates its errno before the separate 64-bit-count semantic bound is checked.
Parsing the cluster count can fail; ext4 returns the error before checking it against the group's cluster limit or storing it.
Parsing for the unsigned-long attribute can fail; the caller propagates errno and does not assign to the field.
A returned cache entry means it is still in use; eviction waits for references and retries. NULL is deletion or absence and not a cache failure.
The name comparison controls the xattr search ordering and match status; an absent attribute can produce -ENODATA but memcmp has no failure return.
An entry returned from the cache means concurrent reuse of the old xattr block; ext4 uses copy-on-write rather than treating it as an error.
Duplicating the old xattr block can fail to allocate memory; clone_block returns through cleanup with -ENOMEM.
Allocating a scratch buffer for a fresh xattr block can fail; ext4 unwinds the update with -ENOMEM.
Charging quota for the shared xattr block can fail with -EDQUOT; ext4 goes to cleanup before taking journal access for that block.

The xattr path uses a newly allocated block within committed ext4 geometry. sb_getblk uses __GFP_NOFAIL there, making the NULL branch defensive under that geometry. Allocating the filesystem block itself can fail in the preceding call.
The comparison returns whether the requested and cached inline xattr values match; a different value is not a comparison failure.
Attaching quota state can fail when acquiring or reading quota objects; ext4 returns the error before starting the xattr update.
The comparison recognizes the special inline data attribute to leave it in the inode; it reports data equality only.
The returned shared cache entry indicates a live reference; ext4 unlocks the buffer and waits before retrying release rather than reporting a failure.
A cache miss only means there is no entry to mark reusable; the xattr block release can proceed without that cache update.
The verified flag is a fast-path state check; a false result triggers checksum verification and any checksum failure is returned by that later path.
The buffer-head pointer array can fail to allocate when the inline array is insufficient; reading the external value returns -ENOMEM.
Charging the external xattr inode can exceed the inode quota; ext4 immediately returns the failure without reserving data space.
Charging data space can exceed an active quota; ext4 reverses the earlier inode charge and propagates the space allocation error.

The value comparison buffer allocation can fail. The helper releases the cache reference and returns NULL; ext4_xattr_inode_lookup_create then creates a fresh value inode instead of sharing the cached one.
The comparison decides whether the cached external xattr inode has the requested value; mismatch continues the cache search without indicating a comparison failure.
The inode lock query is used in a WARN_ON_ONCE precondition before updating disk size; it is not an operation error.
The xattr-name comparison contributes to a distinct-block result during xattr deduplication; equality or inequality is ordinary data.
Comparing inline values determines if two xattr blocks are equivalent; differing bytes are not a failure of memcmp.
The wrapper can receive -EDQUOT from charging space for the ext4 xattr block; it skips dirtying the inode and propagates the error to block-set cleanup.
The GFP_NOFS allocation of the inode-side xattr search state can fail; the combined allocation check cleans up and returns -ENOMEM.
The GFP_NOFS allocation of the block-side xattr search state can fail; the same cleanup path frees the other temporary objects and returns -ENOMEM.
Allocating a scratch buffer to read the external xattr value can fail; the move operation aborts and returns -ENOMEM after cleanup.
